issues.description: The implementation allocates two full H×W Python lists (grid and dp). For the upper constraint H,W ≤ 3000 this means up to ~9e6 entries per matrix (18e6 Python ints total), which will very likely raise MemoryError or crash the process in typical Python environments. This makes the program non-executable for many valid large inputs (e.g., H=W=3000, N>0) and therefore violates correctness under the problem constraints.

The code uses a dense H×W representation for both the input grid and the DP table. A memory-efficient design (for example, using a set of holed cells plus only one or two DP rows instead of the full DP matrix) would keep time complexity O(HW) but reduce memory to O(W) and is required to reliably run within the stated constraints.

The special-case handling for N == 0 correctly avoids the earlier TLE by using the closed-form/summation formula and returns correct results for empty-hole inputs. This fixes the observed failure mode (large empty grid).

No unit or integration tests were provided in the workspace. Add tests covering: (1) N=0 large grid, (2) small grids with and without holes, (3) worst-case sizes with few holes to verify memory/time behavior.
